# ssh

SSH config assembly from ~/.ssh/config.d, host listing, key generation, and EasySSH-driven inventory refresh.

---

## `ssh_generate_host_config`

Regenerate the ssh config fragment for one AWS account/region using easyssh, then rebuild ~/.ssh/config. Credentials are read from ~/.aws/keys/<account>, which must be a regular file.

> **⚠ DANGER** — Sources ~/.aws/keys/<account> into the current shell and replaces $SSH_CONFIG_D/<account>-<region>.config, then runs ssh_refresh_config.

**Usage**

```sh
ssh_generate_host_config [account] [region] [port] [ssh-user]
```

**Examples**

```sh
ssh_generate_host_config myaccount us-east-1 22 ubuntu
```

**Requires** `easyssh`, `aws`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/ssh.sh:169`](../../modules/common/ssh.sh#L169)

**See also** `ssh_refresh_config`

## `ssh_generate_key`

Generate a passphrase-less 4096-bit RSA keypair for an application under $SSH_KEYGEN_OUT_DIR (default ~/.ssh/generated, mode 700).

> **⚠ DANGER** — Writes an unencrypted private key to disk. Refuses to overwrite an existing key of the same name.

**Usage**

```sh
ssh_generate_key <application-name>
```

**Examples**

```sh
ssh_generate_key billing-deploy
```

**Requires** `ssh-keygen`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/ssh.sh:102`](../../modules/common/ssh.sh#L102)

---

## `ssh_generate_keys_all`

Generate a keypair for every name in $APPLICATION_LIST.

> **⚠ DANGER** — See ssh_generate_key.

**Usage**

```sh
ssh_generate_keys_all
```

**Examples**

```sh
APPLICATION_LIST="billing search" ssh_generate_keys_all
```

**Requires** `ssh-keygen`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/ssh.sh:124`](../../modules/common/ssh.sh#L124)

**See also** `ssh_generate_key`

## `ssh_refresh_config`

Rebuild ~/.ssh/config from the fragments in $SSH_CONFIG_D. The previous config is kept as a timestamped backup next to it, so a mistaken run is always recoverable. Explicit command only — this is never run automatically.

> **⚠ DANGER** — Replaces ~/.ssh/config. Hand edits made directly to that file are lost; put them in $SSH_CONFIG_D/*.config instead. A backup is written to ~/.ssh/config.<timestamp>.bak first.

**Usage**

```sh
ssh_refresh_config
```

**Examples**

```sh
ssh_refresh_config
```

**Requires** `ssh`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/ssh.sh:30`](../../modules/common/ssh.sh#L30)

**See also** `ssh_generate_host_config`

## `ssh_start_x2x`

Share this machine's keyboard and mouse with a remote X display over ssh, using x2x.

**Usage**

```sh
ssh_start_x2x [host] [user] [direction] [display]
```

**Examples**

```sh
ssh_start_x2x 192.0.2.10 remoteuser east :0.0
```

**Requires** `ssh`, `x2x`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/ssh.sh:149`](../../modules/common/ssh.sh#L149)
